correctness.rationale: Hölder normalization gives R_j(r)=∫p_j^β r^{1−β}dμ, β=(d+1)/(d−1). The shape-operator perturbation S=I−ε(∇²_S f+fI)+O(ε²) yields p_j=1−ε(d−j+1)/(d+1)(g−E g)+O(ε²), g=(Δ_S+d−1)f. Exact weighted Hölder dual for the two extreme j gives a lower quadratic coefficient β(β−1)||u_+−u_-||²/8; the geometric-mean common density gives the matching upper coefficient because all other u_j lie on the endpoint segment. This is the infimum over all admissible r, not a finite-grid optimization. Harmonic eigenvalues yield V_f=Σ_{ℓ≥2}[ℓ(ℓ+d−2)−(d−1)]²||f_ℓ||², with sharp degree-two constant; independently verified d=3,P₂,J={1,2,3} coefficient exactly 1/5 and three shrinking-ε numerical risk coefficients 0.21551, 0.20820, 0.20420. The O(ε³) claim uses fixed C⁴ f and local smoothness. Finite quadrature is not the d-uniform proof.

originality.rationale: Hoehner's updated arXiv:2602.18547v2 (2026-10-13), Proposition 3.5 and Theorem 3.6, ALREADY prove the exact average-of-two normalized Hölder infimum Z^β and its lower bound on maximum; these portions are prior, not new. Its Remark 3.7 explicitly disclaims the minimum of the maximum. The final submitted result adds the SHARP local minimax equality with a constructed upper bound, the entire d≥3 spherical-harmonic Hessian and the reduction from an arbitrary set of indices to its extrema. The published 2D ellipse minimax is a restricted object and does not dominate the all-dimensional theorem. The source's citation to Hoehner v1 omits this important v2 update; the full scientific novelty is narrowed to the stated exact local quadratic minimax/spectrum, without crediting the lower bound as original. Possible implicit derivations from general perturbation principles remain a residual risk.
